chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has graciously bestowed upon His servants three things: He cast upon them the wind after the spirit, and were it not for that, no dear one would bury a dear one; and He cast upon them solace after calamity, and were it not for that, offspring would be cut off; and He cast upon this grain the creeping creature, and were it not for that, their kings would hoard it just as they hoard gold and silver.

key_terms.الدَّابَّةَ: the creeping creature or pest placed upon grain
key_terms.الرِّيحَ: the wind sent after death, easing the condition of the body
key_terms.السَّلْوَةَ: consolation and forgetfulness that follows calamity
key_terms.النَّسْلُ: human offspring and continuation of lineage
key_terms.الْمُصِيبَةِ: a calamity or affliction that befalls a person
key_terms.يَكْنِزُونَ: they hoard and store up wealth

ai.seo_question: What three worldly favors from Allah does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام mention in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام describes three divine favors bestowed upon humanity in worldly life. The hadith points to Allah’s mercy in making death bearable, grief endurable, and staple food accessible rather than endlessly hoarded.
